newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes stronger, narrow arb bolsters grades.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes stronger, narrow arb bolsters grades.

text.p: U.S. crudes ended the week stronger, underpinned on the cash side by narrow arbitrage between West Texas Intermediate and Brent, giving domestic grade differentials a boost, traders said.
Outright crude values ended stronger as well. NYMEX November crude found support from an unlikely source of late, as unleaded gasoline rallied off lower refiner run rates.
November WTI/Cushing ended at $24.60-70, 40 cts stronger than the Thursday close.
Inter-month November/December WTI moved to just a 29 cts edge for the front month, a bearish signal, traders said.

Light Lousiana Sweet/St. James has been the most obvious sign of the bullish grade stance, attracting refiner interest due to the steep prices for West African parcels and the closed arbitrage for North Sea barrels.
Traders said the latest deals in the LLS were at 63 cts over WTI/Cushing, down 2 cts from the highest price of day, but 10-13 cts higher than deals seen at the start of the week.
Heavy Lousiana Sweet/Empire joined LLS as being a favorite Friday, getting done at 45 cts over WTI/Cushing.
Sour grades ended talked at minus $1.35-$1.32 for West Texas Sour/Midland, and Eugene Island at minus $1.05-$1.02.
November Postings Plus was the weakest segment of the market, remaining between $2.02-$2.06, steady from Thursday.
In the U.S. aftermarket window, Brent paper deals saw December outright sell at $23.70 and $23.69, more than 20 cts higher than the IPE settlement at $23.48.
Traders said there was also a November/December spread done at plus 35 cts.
